title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The sheet is the verso of a typescript page of SGA 7 Exposé IX (p. 136/432, on Néron models and monodromy pairings). The neighbouring pages are typescript, not part of the handwritten notes. The handwriting belongs to Grothendieck's preparation of his 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. There are three layers.

(1) Top, struck through: a fragment of an argument on fibred topoi. The formula τ^α(F) = |α|^*(σ^α(F)) is said to be 'evident' because the σ^α commute with finite and arbitrary limits. A sketch follows of a pro-object 𝔛' = lim 𝔛_𝒰 → X, with induced topoi F/X_i, Δ/𝔛_i, transition maps 𝔛_i ↪ 𝔛_j and restrictions F_i ← F_j. This is routine bookkeeping for computing cohomology of a limit of (hyper)coverings, and it is cancelled.

(2) Middle: 'Démonstration de la formule de Stokes'. Grothendieck introduces maps K_n. Their source is the degree-n part of a PD de Rham object A_n(S, s^+, γ_*, t), evaluated on k'-points. Their target is the completed PD de Rham complex of the standard algebraic n-simplex, Â_n(s^{k'}, ...)^n. The second written form, V(S[Y_0,…,Y_n][[Y_0,…,Y_n]]^{(n)})(k'), suggests the following reading:
- an 'n-chain' is a point of the linear scheme V(·), i.e. a linear form on top-degree PD forms on the simplex with coordinates Y_0,…,Y_n;
- K_n is the canonical 'fundamental chain', a PD analogue of integration over Δ^n.
The Stokes formula to be proved is K^n(dω) = K^{n-1}(∂ω), equivalently dK_n = ∂_{SS} K_{n-1}. Here d_{A^*} raises cohomological degree by 1, and ∂_{SS} is the alternating sum of simplicial face maps. This is stated as commutativity of the square S →K_n (A^*)_n, d_{A^*} down, K_{n-1} down, ∂_{SS} across. The proof plan is induction: '1) it is the identity for n=0', '2) …' (left unfinished).

(3) Bottom: the purpose of the formula. It gives comparison chain maps
C^sing_*(𝔛, k) → C^DR_*(𝔛; s, s^+, γ_*, t)
and
C^sing_*(𝔛, k[𝒰]) → C^{DR,A^1}_*(𝔛, k).
In words, 'algebraic singular chains', built from maps of standard algebraic simplices Spec k[Y_0..Y_n]/(ΣY_i − 1) into 𝔛, map to 'de Rham chains', i.e. duals of PD de Rham cochains. Stokes guarantees that this is a map of complexes. In modern terms this is a period/integration pairing between algebraic singular homology (Suslin-type, built on the cosimplicial scheme Δ^•) and PD/crystalline-type de Rham cohomology. The aim would be an integral or characteristic-p de Rham theorem using divided powers.
errors: The proof of Stokes is only begun: step 2) of the induction is blank, and the indexing in the commutative square is inconsistent. The square goes (A*)_{n-1} → (A*)_{n-1} via ∂_SS, while the struck variant reads dK_n = K_{n+1}∂_SS. This is a draft, not a finished argument.

Caution: a naive 'integration' of PD monomials over Δ^n gives ∫ γ_{a_0}(Y_0)…γ_{a_n}(Y_n) dY = 1/(Σa_i+n)!, which is not integral. So K_n cannot simply be classical integration of PD forms if integrality is wanted. Presumably it is a formal or dual construction (a point of V(·)), and the page does not make this explicit.
Degree annotation: ∂_SS is written with 'deg ss +1', whereas the simplicial boundary lowers simplicial degree. This is only a convention or sign issue in the draft.

ideas.what: Commutation of σ^α / τ^α with limits; pro-system of hypercovering topoi 𝔛' = lim 𝔛_𝒰 → X (struck through)
ideas.modern_name: cohomological descent along pro-hypercoverings / fibred topoi

ideas.what: Fundamental chains K_n on the algebraic n-simplex with values in completed PD de Rham forms, satisfying Stokes dK_n = ∂ K_{n-1}
ideas.modern_name: integration/Stokes map for (PD) polynomial forms on simplices; simplicial de Rham theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational polynomial forms, 1977); Cartan/Thom-Whitney; integral/PD variants Cenkl–Porter (c.1981), Cartier
ideas.where_published: unpublished; 1976 IHÉS talk not written up as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Comparison chain map from algebraic singular chains (maps of algebraic simplices, also an A^1-variant with coefficients k[𝒰]) to PD de Rham chains of 𝔛 over (S, s^+, γ, t)
ideas.modern_name: period pairing between Suslin/algebraic singular homology and de Rham/crystalline cohomology; A^1-singular chains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Suslin–Voevodsky (algebraic singular homology, 1990s); Kontsevich–Zagier/Ayoub style periods; crystalline comparison: Berthelot–Ogus

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an algebraic Stokes formula for a 'fundamental chain' K_n of the standard algebraic simplex. Its values lie in a completed divided-power de Rham complex. He intends to use it to build a chain map from algebraic singular chains to PD de Rham chains, a kind of integral or characteristic-free de Rham theorem. The proof is left at step 2).
missed.quote: Démonstration de la formule de Stokes ... dK_n = ∂_SS K_{n-1} ... C^sing_*(𝔛,k) → C^DR_*(𝔛; s,s^+,γ_*,t)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Pairing algebraic (Suslin-type, Δ^•-based) singular chains with PD/crystalline de Rham cohomology, with an A^1 variant, prefigures interests in A^1-homotopy and in integral or p-adic period pairings. A worked-out version from 1976 would be a historical precedent that is not in the record.

missed.claim: The page links the cosimplicial algebraic simplex Spec k[Y_0..Y_n]/(ΣY−1), later central in Suslin–Voevodsky A^1-homology, with divided-power de Rham theory, via a 'k[𝒰]'/A^1-coefficient singular complex.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would show Grothendieck using algebraic singular chains on Δ^n_alg, with an A^1-flavoured variant, in a comparison with de Rham theory well before the A^1 literature. The page is too fragmentary to establish this firmly.

deep.surprise_reason: Simplicial polynomial forms with Stokes formulas are standard (Sullivan, Cartan, Cenkl–Porter). However, an unpublished 1976 Grothendieck attempt to compare algebraic singular chains on algebraic simplices with PD de Rham chains, including an A^1 variant, is a notable undocumented detail. The content is fragmentary and the proof unfinished.
transcription_corrections: The typed text from the previous and next pages is SGA 7 typescript. This page's handwriting is on the verso of typescript p.136 (432).
'A_n^n([-$-], s^+, γ_*, t)(k)' should read approximately 'A_n^n(S, s^+, γ_*, t)(k')', with S a base or scheme letter, not '$'.
'C^sing_*(𝔛, [-$-]k)' should read 'C^sing_*(𝔛, k)', with an initial letter crossed out.
Superscript on the second DR chain complex: 'DR A^1' appears written over a crossed symbol; plausibly 'DR, A^1'.
The annotation under ∂_SS reads 'deg ss +1' (as written), and under d_{A*} 'degré coh. +1'.
